The C1 Bel Canto Classic Negroni applies the same philosophy. The guilloché-finished platine draws its colour from that iconic deep scarlet vermouth, but it doesn't stay still. Turn your wrist, change the light, and the hue shifts – deep Campari red warming to amber, then to the dark ruby of a freshly poured glass. This is what we mean by bittersweet. A watch that reveals more the longer you look.

sections.bodyEn: The sapphire bezel isn’t just lustrous, but also incredibly tough, and engineered to function at 300m underwater.
Sapphire The sapphire countdown bezel adds a refined sheen without compromising toughness. It’s engineered to provide the perfect ‘click’.

Few complications feel as practical, or as quietly satisfying, as a True GMT. Built for those who cross borders and time zones, it allows the local hour hand to jump independently while a fourth hand keeps track of home, and the date looks after itself, moving forwards or backwards. Elegant, intuitive, and wonderfully mechanical, it’s long been regarded as the most refined expression of the travel watch. But for any brand, creating one from scratch is no small undertaking.
Conceived by technical director Frank Stelzer, it’s built on the foundations of Calibre CW-001 – formerly ‘Calibre SH21’ – the five-day, twin-barrelled movement we launched in 2014.

The first True GMT calibre from a British brand, CW-002 is COSC-certified and joins the small, elite circle of GMT movements. Built on CW-001, it integrates a new GMT mechanism without increasing movement height.
40.5mm Light-catcher™ case with box-domed sapphire crystals front and back, alternating brushed and polished surfaces, and balanced proportions for everyday comfort.
Diamond-polished hour, minute, and small seconds hands, all filled with Super-LumiNova® for low-light legibility; GMT hand and power-reserve indicator lacquered for contrast.

Partially open and deliberately layered, the dial prioritises local time and home time while recessing secondary indicators. Small seconds, power reserve, date, and exposed GMT bridge add depth and utility.
Rhodium-plated movement with circular Côtes de Genève, visible twin barrels and balance wheel, and a tungsten rotor with sunray-polished and sandblasted surfaces.
Applied markers, polished and faceted, filled with Super-LumiNova® for clear visibility in all conditions.

A perfectly proportioned 39mm Light-catcher™ case, a dial to sit and admire, and an hourly spectacle that reignites the mechanical fascination in every watch enthusiast. It must be the C1 Jump Hour Mk V.

The leap towards precision — The jump hour complication is curious in its execution of displaying time. JJ01, developed by former Christopher Ward Master Watchmaker Johannes Jahnke, draws a measured amount of power to create a sharp and instantaneous jump, delivering exceptional timekeeping.

Christopher Ward’s first in-house module, JJ01 was something that had long frustrated master watchmaker Johannes Jahnke. With most jumping hours, the hour number would never flip over exactly as the minute hand passed the hour mark. But his design would be different: it would distribute the power needed to jump the disk across the full hour, rather than a short build-up towards its end, making for a just-so turnover.

The lume-filled handset delivers clarity and precision, while the ‘5N gold’ indexes – also filled with Super-LumiNova® – boast diamond-polished facets that catch the light. The date wheel at 6 o’clock is colour-matched to the dial, while the applied twin-flags logo – also in 5N gold – adds balance and depth.
This means it has a certified timing tolerance of just -4/+6 seconds per day in a variety of temperatures and positions, putting it in the top six percent of Swiss-made watches for accuracy.

The stunning Trident GMT 300 sees the much-anticipated return of the GMT complication to Christopher Ward’s signature ‘Trident’ series, and allows you to monitor up to three separate time zones from your wrist. To see a GMT watch once more in the Trident stable is a reminder of the complication’s popularity with fans since the first Trident GMT appeared in 2009.

Just 4.1mm thick, the SW330-2 has 25 jewels and beats at a rate of 28,800 per hour with a power reserve of up to 56 hours. The central GMT hand can be set independently from the hour and seconds hands.

Look through the sapphire dial and case back, and you’ll see how the finishing – created on the Elara NS CNC milling machine – makes this architecture of CW-001 a feast for the eyes. You can even see the twin barrels, and winding mechanism at 3 o’clock.

On the C60 Trident Lumière, the chamfered indexes are made entirely from Globolight XP©, as is the unmistakable ‘twin flags’ logo and most of the handset. In all, 17 specially-shaped blocks of Globolight XP© are used on the dial which contains five times the lume of any previous Trident (and which cost four times more to produce than a ‘regular’ dial). And because the dial comes in three extraordinary colour options – and whose ‘stippled grain’ surface adds extra texture – there’ll be a shade that’s right for you.

Christopher Ward's first free-sprung balance wheel watch, The C12 Loco, is the most ambitious piece we’ve ever created, demanding not just top-notch design and detailing, but also a brand-new in-house movement, to make it possible.

Architecture and artistry For all its intricate, whirring elegance, you never for one moment forget that The C12 Loco is a sports watch, with everything that implies: technical ability; a crisp, clean contemporary confidence. It’s nothing less than the spiritual child of Louis Cartier and Le Corbusier working in unlikely but delightful harmony…

The earth’s nearest celestial neighbour has long been a subject of fascination for elite watchmakers – including Christopher Ward. After 2015’s C9 Moonphase and 2019’s C1 Moonglow, we present our third and most ambitious moon watch yet: the C1 Moonphase.

Unlike most moonphase complications that transition once per day, JJ04 offers a more dynamic approach. Using the Sellita SW220 as a base, the date wheel, along with its spring-loading assembly, have been stripped out and replaced by four further wheels to drive the moon disc, with two more required for the setting mechanism.

sections.bodyEn: Christopher Ward doesn’t do luxury. Tool watches, yes. Innovative complications, of course. Value for money, most certainly. But luxury – with its show-off implications and forced scarcity – we’ve largely shied away from. If we were to approach this world at all, it would be on our own terms.

And while the Atoll uses the super-slim C60 Trident Pro 300 as its template, this is a timing instrument with its own personality and aesthetic.

So when Christopher Ward set out to create a watch that paid tribute to the Army, Navy and Royal Air Force, we knew that precision timing was front and centre. We also knew that a standard three-hander watch wouldn’t be sufficient.
Dial of delights The reverse panda dial boasts three subdials – with the hand of each one coloured to a particular Service: red for the Army; dark blue for the Navy; light blue for the RAF.
The first C65 Sandhurst was an instant hit when it first appeared in 2019.

As with the original, the watch features a genuine super compressor mechanism – invented in the mid-1950s by case manufacturer Ervin Piquerez SA (EPSA) to allow divers to go deeper without their watch malfunctioning. An ultra-thin compression spring – just 300 microns wide – is placed around the perimeter of the case. When a diver descends, it uses water pressure to press the caseback against the O-ring gasket, increasing water-resistance.
This chronometer version has been tested by the Contrôle Officiel Suisse des Chronomètres, in a number of positions and temperatures to ensure precision timekeeping.

Our new Moonphase’s brushed-and-polished C1 Light-catcher™ case is more elegant than ever at its reduced 37mm dimensions, combining style and subtlety in a perfectly balanced package that’s perfect for smaller wrists, or discrete and refined on larger ones.

Built around surely the most romantic of all watch complications, our Moonphase echoes the waxing and waning of the moon with great accuracy – and for a mighty 128 years. For all this time, your watch’s own moons will chart a graceful unbroken journey across the dial’s star-splattered night-time sky.
An Englishman in New York (well, two actually, oh, and a Swiss)– words by Mike France, CEO & co-founder.

The work was undertaken by Paoluzzo, a maker of precision medical, aviation and horological parts.

Nothing demonstrates this better than the oversized twin moons that – thanks to the power of the JJ04 modified movement – rotate around the sapphire dial, following the movements of the real moon accurately for 128 years.

JJ04: perpetually brilliant The C1 Moonglow is powered by CW’s own modular movement, JJ04, which is able to follow the waxing (and waning) of the moon accurately for 128 years. This also allows the watch’s ‘moons’ to chart a continuous, uninterrupted journey across the dial.

One year later, Richard Benc, founder of Studio Underd0g, was asked by Mike France to partner on the next Alliance watch. Soon after, he floated the idea of a pocket watch - and Mike agreed instantly. After all, what better way to shake up a centuries-old format than by pairing it with a movement built for the modern era… and perhaps even wearing it with sneakers? The result is a pocket watch for people who didn’t think they needed a pocket watch. (They do now.)

The Alliance 02 sold out. Every single one of the 100 pieces. In minutes. Which tells you everything you need to know about what happens when Christopher Ward and Studio Underd0g put their heads together and create a pocket watch that doesn't behave like a pocket watch at all.
